{{for| a (possibly non-associative) algebra such that the product ab&nbsp;–&nbsp;ba or ab&nbsp;+&nbsp;ba satisfies a certain identity|Jordan-admissible algebra|Lie-admissible algebra|Malcev-admissible algebra}}

In mathematics, an '''admissible algebra''' is a (possibly non-associative) [[commutative algebra]] whose enveloping [[Lie algebra]] of [[derivation (abstract algebra)|derivations]] splits into the sum of an even and an odd part. Admissible algebras were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Koecher|year=1967}}.
